summary: Implement approval-controlled self-serve flow for ad-hoc Jira/Confluence/Slack project spawns
description: Issue summary: Request to build a gated, auditable self-serve path so engineers can request new project workspaces (Jira project + Confluence space + Slack channel) without manual ticket handoffs. Impact: Current process requires manual SD/IT triage and ad-hoc emails causing 2-5 day turnaround and inconsistent naming/permission patterns. Business rationale: Reduce lead time for new project launches, enforce naming conventions and least-privilege access, and capture automated audit records for compliance. Request: Design and implement a workflow accessible from a lightweight UI (Confluence macro or Slack command) that captures request metadata, runs policy checks, routes for approval (team lead + security for sensitive classifications), provisions resources via existing provisioning bots, and records the full lifecycle in a central audit Confluence page.
request_details: Desired fields captured: project name, short description, owning pod, privacy level (public/internal/strict), data classification tags, initial member list (github/okta groups), retention policy choice. Approval gates: auto-approve for 'public' and 'internal' with owner signoff; require Security review for 'strict' or if data_classification contains PHI/PCI. Provisioning steps: create Jira project from 'team-template' (default issue types and workflows), create Confluence seeded space using 'project-kickoff' template, create Slack channel with naming prefix pod-<pod>-<shortname>, attach onboarding checklist bot and set channel retention policy, create service account with scoped token for bots, and seed runbook under the Confluence space with links to the Jira project and channel. Audit: every provision event must write a line to 'Internal Provisioning Audit' Confluence page and emit an event to ops-telemetry channel (for future telemetry ingestion).
steps_to_execute: Operator steps (for automation implementer): 1) Add a new API endpoint to the provisioning gateway to accept structured requests (JSON). 2) Implement policy evaluation module (name compliance, classification checks, membership sanity). 3) Wire approval flows into Slack modal + Jira for audit (create a lightweight approval ticket). 4) Call existing slack-bot-provisioner to create channel and install onboarding automations. 5) Call confluence-seed job to create space and seed template with variables. 6) Call jira-template-provisioner to create project and apply permission scheme. 7) Emit audit entry and webhook to ops-telemetry. 8) Return provisioned object URLs to requester and create an ephemeral follow-up task for onboarding checklist.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Request UI validates required fields and rejects disallowed names. 2) Policy engine correctly flags 'strict' classifications and prevents auto-approve. 3) Approvals are routed to correct reviewers and decisions are logged. 4) Provisioner creates Jira project, Confluence space, Slack channel, and service account, all with correct naming/permission templates. 5) Audit entry is written and webhook emitted. 6) End-to-end test exists and is runnable by Platform Eng. 7) Documentation for requesters and runbook for operators added to Confluence.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel (reporter): Opening request — small cross-pod teams keep waiting for new projects. Proposed flow should reduce manual steps and centralize audit.

2026-03-11 - Marco Ruiz (assignee): Reviewed high-level ask. Need decision on whether the approval ticket should live in an 'ops-approvals' Jira project or be ephemeral in the provisioning gateway datastore. Leaning towards an ops-project so non-developers can triage.

2026-03-11 - Security (Maya Chen): We require a Security reviewer for any 'strict' or data_classification flagged PHI/PCI. Also request encryption-at-rest verification for service account tokens. Will provide checklist.

2026-03-12 - Platform Eng (Diego Alvarez): Implementation notes: we can reuse the existing confluence-seed lambda and slack-bot-provisioner. Risk: current slack-bot-provisioner creates channels as app-managed owners; need to ensure ownership is transferred or recorded for long-term access. Estimated 3 sprints with one sprint of integration testing.
2026-03-12 - Aisha Patel: Confirmed team lead approver list will be pulled from our team-directory service; will provide API access token to the gateway.
2026-03-12 - Marco Ruiz: Blocking item: need an updated permission scheme for Jira templates to grant project-admin to a role mapped from the owning pod. Filed follow-up (see follow_up_actions).
investigation_notes: Checked current provisioning bots and templates. Found gap: no single source-of-truth for naming rules (some pods use prefix vs suffix). Existing slack-bot-provisioner supports channel creation and apps install but lacks hooking into an approval workflow. Confluence template 'project-kickoff' exists and is suitable with minor variables. Jira permission schemes need minor adjustments to support pod-based admins.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (design): finalize request JSON schema, approval routing, and RBAC mapping (1 week). Phase 2 (build): extend provisioning-gateway API, add policy module, integrate approver routing to ops-approvals Jira project and Slack modals (2 sprints). Phase 3 (test): integration tests and smoke tests in staging with sample pods (1 sprint). Phase 4 (rollout): enable opt-in for a pilot pod and collect feedback, then enable org-wide with telemetry (2 weeks).
rollout_plan: Pilot with two pods (Platform and Developer Experience) for 2 weeks. Monitor provisioning telemetry and support tickets for drift. Gradual ramp: enable new projects for 10% pods after pilot, then 50%, then org-wide. Provide rollback via a deprovision job that can be invoked if naming or permissions are incorrect.
estimated_effort: Design: 8 engineer-days. Implementation: 48 engineer-days across 2 engineers. Testing & documentation: 8 engineer-days. Total: ~7 engineer-weeks of effort spread across team.
blockers: 1) Final sign-off on approval routing (ops-project vs ephemeral). 2) API access to team-directory service for owner resolution. 3) Minor Jira permission scheme change that requires Product Security sign-off.
follow_up_actions: 1) Marco to open INT ticket to modify Jira permission scheme (blocked until security sign-off). 2) Aisha to share team-directory service token with platform-eng sandbox. 3) Security will publish checklist for 'strict' classification reviews. 4) Platform Eng to draft E2E integration tests and a staging runbook.
